meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. That's procedure 4.2, and I'm writing down that you said it. Now, on what basis is there a zero at all?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

A seventeen-year-old saying "like, being stuck" when his teacher springs a vocabulary question on him is not proof of anything. Show me the note you wrote that day. Did you tell Owen on November 2 that his mark was at risk?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what outlines are for. I'm writing down October 15, and I want the outline and the essay side by side in front of me. And whatever comes of this, it stays off Owen's record and it stays quiet.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Thursday at 8:15, in this room, just Owen and you, not in front of his class, and I'll agree to it to put this behind him. But I want that promise in writing before he sits down Thursday, not Friday at 3 PM after the fact. And until then, who else has seen that zero?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will do a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, that the new mark will replace the zero if it holds up, and that nothing will go on his record. I still require that rewrite to be private and not in front of his class, that your promise be put in writing, and that you tell me who else has seen the zero. I expect that promise in writing before Owen sits down on Thursday at 8:15.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15, provided the promise that nothing goes on file is in writing first.
What moved her: the October 15 outline arguing cowardice compared with an essay that never mentions it.
